judged_text: In sharing mode the office365 refresh spreads minimum-schema-parsed data ({access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token"}) over o365AuthCredentials and persists the result via prisma.credential.update. The stored Office365 credential's real refresh_token is replaced by the placeholder string and the stale expiry_date is kept (the expiry field was stripped by the broken schema), so the next refresh POSTs refresh_token=refresh_token to Microsoft and fails permanently; disabling credential sharing later does not bring the lost token back.

record.issue_text: [BUG] In sharing mode the office365 refresh spreads minimum-schema-parsed data ({access_token, refresh_token: "refresh_token"}) over o365AuthCredentials and persists the result via prisma.credential.update. The stored Office365 credential's real refresh_token is replaced by the placeholder string and the stale expiry_date is kept (the expiry field was stripped by the broken schema), so the next refresh POSTs refresh_token=refresh_token to Microsoft and fails permanently; disabling credential sharing later does not bring the lost token back.

adjudication.rationale: In Office365 refresh, the code now calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` and then merges the parsed data into the existing credential (`o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`) before persisting via `prisma.credential.update(...)`. In sharing mode, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` uses `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which does not require/retain `refresh_token`) and then forcibly sets `refresh_token` to the placeholder string when missing: `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`. That placeholder is then spread over and overwrites the real stored refresh token, permanently losing it. Since the minimum schema also may not retain the real expiry field(s), the old expiry can remain. Disabling sharing later would not restore the lost refresh token, so subsequent non-sharing refreshes would fail.
